sources.title: Malaysia Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Country climate-development assessment; observed subnational vulnerabilities and policy recommendations, with modeled future impacts.
sources.methodology: Country assessment using sector analysis, biophysical modeling and government and civil-society consultations.
sources.limitations: Recommendations are not evaluated outcomes; district averages mask local variation.

sources.title: Governing Climate Risks as National Security Priority: Call to Re-examine Malaysia’s Reactive Approach to Environmental Hazards
sources.organization: Institute of Strategic & International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia
sources.temporal_coverage: Research note published in 2026; displacement examples from 2021-24 and conditional future risks.
sources.methodology: Research note synthesizes a 2025 conference, roundtable, official data and published studies.
sources.limitations: Qualitative synthesis; conditional pathways are not measured local violence.

sources.title: Balancing Innovation and Coordination: Institutional Solutions for Effective Climate Action in Malaysia’s Borneo States — Subnational Climate Change Institutional Assessment Overview
sources.organization: World Bank Group, with Sarawak Ministry of Energy and Environmental Sustainability and Sabah Forestry Department
sources.temporal_coverage: Institutional overview published March 2026; describes state structures, tools and capacity constraints.
sources.methodology: State assessment based on institutional review and engagement with government agencies.
sources.limitations: Overview covers Sabah and Sarawak state functions, not national adaptation outcomes.

sources.title: Coping with Climate Change: OECD Economic Surveys: Malaysia 2026
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 economic survey chapter; includes first-half 2026 agricultural impacts and current policy status.
sources.methodology: Country economic survey chapter synthesizing official statistics and cited research.
sources.limitations: Some event and projection findings are cited from other institutions.

claims.paraphrase: Flood and poverty exposure overlap in Sarawak’s Kanowit, Kapit, Sibu and Song districts and coastal Sandakan, Semporna, Sabak Bernam and Batu Pahat; poorer households have weaker housing and fewer savings or insurance.
claims.limitations: District correlations can mask within-area exposure.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report warns that unequal climate exposure may reinforce subnational economic disparities.

claims.paraphrase: Climate planning faces weak participation, low climate knowledge and public-trust concerns.
claims.limitations: The report describes constraints, not measured participation outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It states weak social cohesion and unequal norms can undermine collective climate action.

claims.paraphrase: Indigenous land-tenure insecurity in Sabah and Sarawak leaves customary rights contested and undermines forest governance and conservation.
claims.limitations: The passage does not establish an armed-conflict link.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report explicitly links tenure insecurity with weaker forest governance and conservation.

claims.paraphrase: The CCDR proposes targeted housing, livelihood and financial support for poorer flood-prone communities and climate planning with women, youth, Orang Asli and other Indigenous peoples.
claims.limitations: These are recommendations, not evidence of delivered capacity.

claims.paraphrase: Floods displaced 129,000 people in 2021 and 156,000 in 2022, concentrated in five states; poorer Klang Valley households can be trapped in repeated evacuations.
claims.limitations: Displacement totals are historical and reported through the note’s cited sources.

claims.paraphrase: Climate displacement can remove legal, social and economic protections that otherwise contain resource competition and social tension; children, women and elders face higher risks.
claims.limitations: The note identifies a qualitative pathway, not observed local violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: ISIS explicitly says protection loss can allow resource competition and social tensions to escalate.

claims.paraphrase: With no displacement or refugee legal protection, future climate-displaced people could lack recognition and services and face tensions with host communities and the state.
claims.scenario: The note presents a conditional future risk and specifies no climate or demographic scenario.
claims.limitations: Conditional qualitative pathway, not a measured future outcome.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The note links legal exclusion and temporary displacement policy to resource competition and tensions.

claims.paraphrase: Sabah’s climate governance is centralized in the Chief Minister’s Department; Sabah and Sarawak have overlapping mandates and silos that impede coordination.
claims.limitations: Planned Climate Change Centers were not yet established in this overview.

claims.paraphrase: Sabah uses iForSABAH, GeoForest and forest-fire danger maps, while both Borneo states report technical and budget gaps in climate monitoring.
claims.limitations: The overview does not evaluate resulting risk reduction.

claims.locator: Full-report chapter, “Coping with Climate Change,” paragraph beginning “During the first half of 2026”.
claims.paraphrase: During the first half of 2026, dry spells lowered paddy yields by over 60% in areas of Kedah, Perlis and Perak.
claims.limitations: The chapter does not disaggregate affected localities within the states.

claims.locator: Full-report chapter, “Coping with Climate Change,” paragraphs under “Developing a national climate change adaptation strategy”.
claims.paraphrase: The late-2024 National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030 decentralizes risk management, but local human and financial shortages hinder implementation.
claims.limitations: Policy adoption does not establish implementation results.

claims.locator: Full-report chapter, “Coping with Climate Change,” paragraphs beginning “Despite the ongoing policy initiatives” and “The national government is still working”.
claims.paraphrase: Adaptation policies remain fragmented across ministries and sectors; Malaysia’s National Adaptation Plan is still under development.
claims.limitations: The chapter reports policy status as of 2026, not later implementation.

search_audit.query: Malaysia climate vulnerability flood Sabah Sarawak indigenous communities World Bank report PDF
search_audit.outcome: Found opened World Bank reports with poverty and flood exposure in named Sarawak and Sabah districts and state-level adaptation evidence.

search_audit.query: Malaysia climate security conflict climate change social cohesion Sabah Sarawak report primary
search_audit.outcome: ISIS Malaysia’s directly opened research note identifies displacement-protection gaps and conditional pathways to resource competition and social tension; it does not establish climate-caused armed violence.

search_audit.query: Malaysia climate change flood conflict land rights displacement insecurity adaptation indigenous report World Bank UNDP
search_audit.outcome: The opened CCDR says Indigenous tenure insecurity undermines forest governance; no inspected source demonstrates active insecurity disrupting adaptation or causing violence.

search_audit.query: Malaysia resilience capacity climate adaptation flood Sabah Sarawak official report
search_audit.outcome: Found state forest-monitoring tools and identified coordination, technical and local fiscal/staff capacity constraints; proposals are not treated as delivered capacity.

gaps: No inspected source establishes climate stress as the cause of organized armed violence in Malaysia; ISIS describes conditional displacement-related social-tension pathways.
The reviewed evidence does not show active insecurity disrupting climate adaptation; the Indigenous tenure finding concerns governance and conservation.
The full World Bank Flood Risk Management report PDF exceeded the fetch limit; its landing-page summary and search snippets were not used.
The 2026 institutional overview covers Sabah and Sarawak, not the national climate-adaptation system; proposed Climate Change Centers were not yet established.
World Bank CCDR recommendations are proposals, not evidence that services or resilience measures have been delivered.
